title: Prove runtime operations never alter the saved Scene

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0060 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive to close the last uncited-criteria node. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0060.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: AC-013's 'runtime edits never alter a saved Scene without an explicit save-back' was proven only for the in-memory scene object at the unit tier, not against a saved CollectionRecord re-read from storage. The isolation held by convention because ProductionService.loadPreview prepares and clones the scene, but there was no persistence-tier proof.
claims.evidence: server/src/services/ProductionService.ts loadPreview and prepareScene, and the prior coverage audit of AC-013.

claims.statement: The change adds a persistence-tier proof that after Preview load, controls and Take against a saved Scene, the saved CollectionRecord re-read from storage is byte-identical to its saved form; getCollection returns the stored record by reference, so any aliasing mutation would surface. No product code changes.

AC-016's device-token least-privilege (a token executes only its selected actions for its Show, and cross-Show, undeclared, expired and revoked actions are denied) is already proven at the integration tier by the device-credential HTTP tests; only surfacing device tokens through the Studio Integrations UI remains.

Governed discovery reordered the work: AC-013's gap was a missing persistence-tier proof, not a missing isolation guarantee, so the slice adds a re-read comparison rather than changing the ProductionService.
claims.evidence: Governed-discovery reorder check on 2026-08-24 and the loadPreview cloning path.

claims.statement: Exercising Preview load, controls and Take against a saved Scene and asserting the re-read CollectionRecord is byte-identical, while Preview and Program advance, proves AC-013's saved-source isolation.

Human review accepted CHG-0060: after Preview load, controls and Take against a saved Scene, the saved CollectionRecord re-read from storage is byte-identical, proving AC-013's runtime isolation at the persistence tier. AC-016's device-token least-privilege is already proven at the integration tier; the Integrations UI stays deferred.
claims.evidence: server/tests/unit/runtimeSceneIsolation.test.ts, the passing full server suite under npm run check, the CHG-0060 pull-request Constitution run, and human acceptance on 2026-08-24.

claims.statement: The change is test-only; no product or protocol behavior changes.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0060 branch and the pull-request validate job.

claims.statement: Surfacing device tokens through the Studio Integrations UI (AC-016 UI half) remains a placeholder and is deferred to a successor.
